note: Attacker-controlled bytes are copied into the JS source buffer that drives Hermes parsing and string conversion.
The input length and byte range are propagated into the UTF-8 to UTF-16 string construction path.
The conversion buffer is sized only to the input byte length, which can be insufficient for the resulting UTF-16 output when the input contains multi-byte UTF-8 sequences.
The UTF-8 to UTF-16 conversion writes through the fixed-size target buffer and can overrun it, producing the stack-buffer-overflow read/write reported by ASan.
